claim: CRITICAL: Quartz bitmap context draws pixels vertically upside down. In Core Graphics the default coordinate system of a `CGBitmapContext` places the origin (0,0) at the bottom-left corner with Y pointing upward, while the raw buffer returned by `CGBitmapContextGetData` lays pixel rows top-to-bottom starting at row 0. `core/src/imageio.rs` passes the `CGImage` directly to `CGContextDrawImage` without flipping the context transformation matrix, so it renders the image vertically inverted into the pixel array: any valid HEIC (e.g. an iPhone photo) comes out as a JPEG flipped along the Y axis.
refutation_private: Portrait output viewed upright; ImageIO reads every output at orientation 1; a strengthened row test passes on the unchanged drawing code; the prescribed CTM flip would have inverted the image.

claim: Multi-image HEIC: index 0 is the primary by spec. `CGImageSourceGetCount >= 1` and `CreateImageAtIndex(0)` in `core/src/imageio.rs` is right for burst, live photo and animated HEIF, because the primary is item 0 in the `pitm` sense, and `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(0)` on a container with a `thmb` item returns the primary, not the thumb.
refutation_private: pitm need not be item 0; CGImageSourceGetPrimaryImageIndex exists for exactly that, and DeepSeek's own failing case (item 0 a preview, picture at index 1) contradicts its heading.

claim: The byte order is a constant, not the platform's: `core/src/imageio.rs` passes `K_CG_IMAGE_ALPHA_NONE_SKIP_LAST | K_CG_BITMAP_BYTE_ORDER_DEFAULT` with `K_CG_BITMAP_BYTE_ORDER_DEFAULT = 0`. The value is a literal while the constant's name says "the platform's default", so the R,G,B,X layout the engine reads is not actually tied to the host's byte order.
refutation_private: 0 is Apple's kCGBitmapByteOrderDefault; the layout is correct on every Mac (all little-endian) and the module is cfg-gated macOS-only; nothing to change.

claim: `CGContextDrawImage` does not colour-convert when the context uses the image's own space. For a Display P3 source in `core/src/imageio.rs`, `ctx_cs` is the image's `CGColorSpace` and the context is 8 bpc; if Image I/O hands back a `CGImage` with extended-range components, values above 1.0 clamp to the per-component max. A real iPhone HDR HEIC decoded by Image I/O as extended range will clamp and bleed at exactly the highlights the Email preset exists to show.
refutation_private: The primary item of an iPhone HEIC is SDR; the HDR range lives in the gain map, which the engine reports as dropped.

claim: In `core/src/webp.rs`, `PICTURE_CHUNKS` includes `b"VP8X"`, but `VP8X` is the extended feature header, not an image frame bitstream. `VP8X` should be removed from `PICTURE_CHUNKS` so that `has_picture` strictly requires a true frame (`VP8 ` or `VP8L`); every WebP that carries pixels has one of those two chunks at the top level of its RIFF chain.
refutation_private: An animated WebP has neither VP8 nor VP8L at top level (pixels live in ANMF; Pillow writes VP8X,ANIM,ANMF...), so the proposed fix would break stripping animated files.

claim: Clearing the VP8X flags at `out[20]` in `strip_webp` (`core/src/webp.rs`) is safe and correct. Per the WebP container spec `VP8X` must be the first chunk, so the RIFF header is bytes 0..12, the `VP8X` chunk header is bytes 12..20, and the first payload byte holding the feature flags is exactly `out[20]`. The `out.len() > 20` guard prevents out-of-bounds indexing if `VP8X` has a zero-length payload or is cut short, and `&out[12..16] == b"VP8X"` ensures the flags are only modified when `VP8X` is in the first-chunk position.
refutation_private: With a zero-length VP8X, out[20] is the next kept chunk's FourCC; clearing the bits renames 'VP8 ' to 'RP8 ' (reproduced by test an_empty_extended_header_does_not_get_its_neighbour_renamed).

claim: A WebP containing a picture chunk with a zero-length payload returns `Some` from `strip_webp` (`core/src/webp.rs`) with `wiped > 0`, so the `lib.rs` branch never sees `wiped == 0` and happily emits a "stripped" WebP with a blank picture, which `Source::open` then decodes to an image of nothing through an `unwrap_or`-style fallback rather than reporting the blank. `has_picture` needs a payload-length floor.
refutation_private: Reading image-webp: it bounds its walk by riff_size and returns typed errors for such files rather than decoding to nothing.

claim: The profile is read through the same torn chain: `icc_profile` in `core/src/webp.rs` swallows the walk's `None` and returns `None`, which is indistinguishable from "this file carries no `ICCP`". A wide-gamut WebP cut short in transit therefore loses its profile and comes back untagged, flat, and reported as a success.
refutation_private: Real in shape but unreachable: image-webp refuses the torn file before the untagged result could be written.

claim: Fast-mode PDF rewrites run at core count: `concurrencyLimit` in `app/Sources/JobQueue.swift` returns `cores` unless some job is `.quality`, and a PDF through Shrink is `.fast`, so a batch of PDFs on a 16 GB / 8-core machine runs eight concurrent document rewrites, each holding every decoded picture in a document at once. The 167 MB-per-fast-job figure the concurrency limit rests on was measured for single images, so a PDF batch can exceed it.
refutation_private: core/src/pdf.rs rewrite iterates candidates one at a time (decode, encode, replace stream before the next); measured 61 MB max RSS on a fast-mode PDF.

claim: `public.heif` likely re-admits AVIF: Apple's UTI tree conforms `public.avif` to `public.heif`, so declaring `public.heif` on the Convert to AVIF Services entry (`app/project.yml`) probably makes Finder offer Convert to AVIF for `.avif` files despite the exclusion, a menu item that always reports failure.
refutation_private: UTType.conforms on macOS 27: public.avif -> public.heif is false (both conform to public.heif-standard), as recorded in project.yml; the live run on an .avif went through NSPerformService, which does not filter by declared type.

claim: `concurrencyLimit` keys on `job.mode` (`app/Sources/JobQueue.swift`). If `Job` stores a separate `mode` that defaults to `.fast` for preset-created jobs rather than returning `preset.mode`, an AVIF batch runs at core-count concurrency with quality-mode memory, the exact blowup the limit exists to prevent.
refutation_private: Job.mode is a computed property returning preset.mode (Job.swift:24).

claim: Silent semantic loss: `org.webmproject.webp` includes animated WebP and `public.heif` includes HEIF sequences, so converting either through Convert to AVIF yields a still AVIF, silently dropping every frame after the first.
refutation_private: optimize_as refuses both with Error::ReadOnlyFormat before any decoder runs (webp::is_animated and heif::is_image_sequence checks in lib.rs); nothing is written.

claim: The `landsOnSource` comparison in `app/Sources/JobQueue.swift` is lexical, not filesystem identity. Unicode-normalisation aliases could therefore be a false negative if Foundation constructs the destination with a different normalisation from the source and the volume resolves both to the same entry, letting a conversion be written over its own source.
refutation_private: destination is built from the same URL (deletingLastPathComponent + stem + extension); both sides carry identical bytes for every component except the extension, and no normalisation is introduced on either side.

claim: The queue does not compare `result.data` with the input before writing and marking the job done (`app/Sources/JobQueue.swift`). If an engine mode can succeed with byte-identical output, for example Strip on a file with nothing removable, the app still performs a write and reports completion.
refutation_private: optimize_as returns Error::NoSmallerResult from every strip path when nothing was removed (wiped == 0 for HEIF/TIFF/GIF/WebP, metadata_removed == 0 for PDF, stripped.len() >= bytes.len() for JPEG/PNG); the app maps it to 'nothing to remove'.

claim: The new inline JSON-LD is probably blocked by the CSP, and fails silently. `index.html:30` adds `<script type="application/ld+json">`; CSP `script-src` applies to inline script elements including non-executable types, so unless `_headers` carries `'unsafe-inline'` or a hash for this block, Chrome and Firefox refuse it and the Person schema never reaches a crawler, with no visible symptom and no build failure.
refutation_private: application/ld+json is a data block, not executed script, and is not subject to script-src.

claim: `unlisted` was wired into three consumers and probably not the fourth. `build-blog.mjs` filters `listed` for the index and blog feed, and `build-search-index.mjs` filters it out of search, but `scripts/build-feed.mjs` is unchanged and, if it reads `pages.json`, the superseded post enters the site release feed and reaches every subscriber at `/feed.xml`, exactly the exposure `unlisted` exists to prevent.
refutation_private: The unlisted 2025 highlights post is absent from /feed.xml and /blog/feed.xml; build-feed.mjs builds a site-change feed and does not read the blog's pages.json.

claim:
`indentOutsidePre()` in `scripts/build-blog.mjs` evaluates `inPre` before updating state for the current line. On the line opening `
`, `inPre` is false, so the line gets indented by 12 spaces; on the closing `
` line, `inPre` is true, so it receives no indentation. Multi-line `
` blocks therefore output misaligned outer tags in the HTML source.
refutation_private: The open line is padded and the close line deliberately not; padding would inject whitespace into the code block. Astra and DeepSeek both read the function as correct.

claim: Tie-breaking in `scripts/build-speaking.mjs` and `scripts/build-ai.mjs` uses `localeCompare()` without an explicit locale parameter (e.g. `a.slug.localeCompare(b.slug)`), so the generated pages can re-order across CI runners or mirrors operating under differing system locales (`LANG`).
refutation_private: The compared ids/slugs are lowercase ASCII and sort identically in every relevant locale (DeepSeek itself said the order is stable today).

claim: Stale state leak on navigation in `src/pages/Jar.tsx`: `details` state is never cleared when `refFilter` changes or is removed (`if (!payments || !refFilter) return`). Navigating from a specific receipt (`?ref=TAB-123`) back to the main jar view leaves stale transaction details in memory, and any matching transaction signatures in the full jar list will erroneously render `<TxShape>` elements despite no reference filter being active.
refutation_private: TxShape is only rendered inside the refFilter block and is looked up by immutable signature; Astra and SWE-2 agreed.

claim: Open-amount URL link param overwrite allows spoofing/underpayment. When a merchant chooses "Whatever the payer chooses, for a tip jar" in `Create.tsx`, the amount is ignored, but a crafted payload with `a` (or `u`) set alongside an open tip-jar request keeps `a` through `normalizeRequest`, and `Pay.tsx` checks `if (request.amount)` before `isOpenAmount(request)`. A link with `a: "0.000001"` therefore tricks a payer viewing an open tip jar into paying 0.000001 COOK instead of their intended tip: the UI's input expectation and the signed amount disagree.
refutation_private: An `a` field makes the link a fixed request and the page renders it as one; the wire format has no separate open/fixed mode flag to contradict.

claim: Multi-account balance consolidation error misleads the payer. `Pay.tsx` displays `holding.spendable` as what the user can send, and `fetchBalanceOf` (`src/lib/balances.ts`) sets `spendable` from the sum of the token accounts, while `chooseSourceAccount` in `src/lib/pay.ts` throws a `PaymentError` when no single account holds `rawAmount`. With 10 tokens in the ATA and 10 in an auxiliary account and a 15-token invoice, the UI allows clicking "Pay 15" but building then fails with "split across 2 accounts... consolidate them first".
refutation_private: spendable is the largest single account (balances.ts:70), matching chooseSourceAccount.

claim: `looksLikeName` / `validateRecipient` (`src/lib/names.ts`, `src/lib/request.ts`) misclassify a base58 address ending in `.cook`: `.cook` is five lowercase characters all in the base58 alphabet, so any 32-44-character key ending in those five characters returns true from `looksLikeName` and is forced down the name path, where `resolveRecipient` throws `not registered` and the recipient can never be paid.
refutation_private: '.' is outside the base58 alphabet, so no base58 address can contain '.cook' (council.probe.ts C-4).

claim: The `fetchJarHistory` prefilter in `src/lib/history.ts` relies on `entry.memo`: the RPC memo summary is treated as authoritative, so a node that does not populate it silently drops every real payment and reports "No Cookie Jar payments have reached this address yet", the one wrong answer the comment above `PAGE` says a jar must never give.
refutation_private: history.ts:147 skips only when entry.memo !== null and lacks the prefix; null-memo entries are kept as candidates by design and re-checked after the full fetch.

claim: `package.json` defines `"live": "tsx scripts/live-check.ts"`, and the README says `npm run live` runs 18 checks against the live chain, but the file `scripts/live-check.ts` does not exist in the repository (the `scripts/` directory is missing), so `npm run live` fails immediately with module not found.
refutation_private: Artifact of the code-only archive staged for that lane, which excluded scripts/; the file exists in the repository at this commit.

claim: Stale payment state can survive a route change. `Pay.tsx`'s initialization effect does not clear `request`, `resolved`, `priceUsd`, `enteredAmount`, or `holding` when `payload` changes; it only sets `stage` to "reading". Navigating from `#/pay/<A>` to `#/pay/<B>` while the component stays mounted and clicking during B's asynchronous load leaves `payBlocker` null on the stale state, and `pay()` can submit A's payment from the B URL.
refutation_private: The sign-time re-resolve in pay() refuses a mismatched request; downgraded to a stale-display issue (Pay.tsx:74-100).

claim: Memo separator injection breaks memo structure. `buildMemo` in `src/lib/request.ts` replaces `|` with `/` in `ref` but does not escape `|` in `note`, so a request with `ref = "INV123"` and `note = "foo|bar"` produces `cookiejar:1|INV123|foo|bar`, and `parseMemo` then splits on the wrong separator and returns a ref and note different from what the link creator set.
refutation_private: ref is escaped and note deliberately takes the remainder after the second separator; parseMemo round-trips the example correctly.

claim: In `buildPayment` (`src/lib/pay.ts`), when the mint is wrapped COOK (`So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112`) the payment is a direct SPL token transfer without unwrapping or handling native lamports, which leaves the funds trapped in a token account if the recipient expected native COOK.
refutation_private: isNative covers the wrapped mint and routes it to SystemProgram.transfer; no SPL transfer is built for it.

claim: History is pre-filtered on the RPC memo summary: the candidate filter in `fetchJarHistory` (`src/lib/history.ts`) drops transactions when `s.memo` is present but not the jar memo, and `getSignaturesForAddress`'s `memo` field is the first memo's summary, so a payment whose jar memo is the second memo instruction can be silently excluded (false negative).
refutation_private: The RPC memo summary includes every memo instruction in the transaction, so a second-instruction jar memo still contains the prefix.

claim: Precision loss in `usdToRaw` (`src/lib/quote.ts`) is a defect: for `usd = "0.01"`, `priceUsd = 1000000` and `decimals = 2`, the fixed-point division evaluates to `0n` and `usdToRaw` throws `QuoteError`, blocking legitimate payments whenever a dollar amount evaluates below one integer base unit.
refutation_private: A sub-unit amount cannot be transferred at all; refusing it with a clear QuoteError is the correct behaviour, not a defect.

claim: `_headers` does not cover the new pages. It grants `max-age=0, must-revalidate` only to `/`, `/morning/`, `/morning/daybreak/`, `/hours/`, `/psalter/` and `/psalter/*`; the pages shipped in the latest releases (`/compline/`, `/evening/rule/`, `/canons/`, `/communion/`, `/communion/canon/`, `/communion/thanksgiving/`) match no rule, so that HTML ships with no Cache-Control at all and browsers may heuristically cache it, serving stale text on first visit before the service worker installs.
refutation_private: Live: all 38 routes send 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' (Cloudflare Pages' HTML default); the proposed /* rule would add a second, contradictory Cache-Control to /fonts/* and /art/*.

claim: In `evening/rule/index.html`, Chrysostom's 24 petitions are wrapped in `<div class="prayer indented">`. The CSS rule `.prayer .prayer.indented` in `prayers.css` requires nesting and fails to match, so only `.prayer.indented p` applies (`text-indent: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0`), and on phone screens multi-line petitions wrap to the left margin while single-line starts indent 1.5em, producing a jagged layout.
refutation_private: The petitions blocks are nested inside an outer .prayer div, so the selector matches; computed 18.4px gap on the preview.

claim: Dead rule in `prayers.css`: `.prayer.indented p.opening { text-indent: 0 }` matches nothing, because the only `.opening` paragraphs are in non-indented `.prayer` blocks.
refutation_private: Used by /morning/daybreak/, which has a .prayer.indented block with an opening paragraph.

claim: `prayers.css` has no `:focus` style on `.prayer a` / `.rubric-line a`, so links have no visible focus indicator: a reader using a Bluetooth keyboard with the phone gets no visible ring as focus moves.
refutation_private: No rule in prayers.css removes the browser's default focus ring (no outline:none), so focus stays visible.
